e: Creating an Aurora PostgreSQL read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL instance keeps it continuously in sync through replication, and promoting it at cutover gives minimal downtime and data loss with little operational work. Snapshot restore, S3 import, or pg_dump all leave a gap of changes or long downtime.

AWS Backup can apply a backup plan to all EC2 instances (using tags or resource assignments) automatically, and its restore can be run through the API or CLI for many instances, requiring the least effort. Custom CloudFormation, Elastic Beanstalk, or Lambda scripts need to be built and maintained.

The Step Functions Map state in Distributed mode processes large datasets in S3 with up to 10,000 parallel child workflow executions, serverless and purpose-built for large-scale parallel processing. Inline mode is limited to 40 concurrent iterations, Glue is for ETL, and custom Lambda orchestration adds work.

At 500 Mbps with 80% usable (400 Mbps), 10 PB would take decades, far beyond 6 weeks, so physical transfer is required: multiple Snowball devices. DataSync, rsync, and the CLI are all limited by the network link.

A cached volume gateway stores the full dataset in S3 and keeps frequently used data in a local cache, giving low-latency access to hot data while reducing the on-premises storage footprint, and it exposes iSCSI volumes with minimal infrastructure change. Stored volumes keep everything on premises.

S3 Standard for the first 30 days, then a lifecycle rule to Standard-IA keeps the multi-AZ durability and immediate availability at any time while lowering cost for rarely accessed older objects. Glacier isn't readily available, One Zone-IA reduces durability, and Intelligent-Tiering adds monitoring fees.

Storing the 6 MB documents as objects in S3 (with metadata in the database) shrinks the database, which improves performance and lowers storage cost, and S3 is highly durable and available. Larger or Magnetic volumes, or DynamoDB (400 KB item limit), don't fix it cost-effectively.

An AWS WAF web ACL associated with the ALB can use IP set rules to allow only the registered IP addresses (and scales to many addresses), blocking everything else. Network ACLs are limited in rule count (20,000 locations is too many), and Firewall Manager or a Lambda authorizer isn't suited.

Lake Formation data filters provide row-level and cell-level (and column-level) security so sensitive portions of the data are hidden from users, managed centrally with the least overhead. IAM roles alone don't restrict parts of tables, and Lambda cleansing functions need custom code.

A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 keeps traffic from the EC2 instances to S3 off the public internet, and Direct Connect gives the on-premises servers a private connection to the VPC (and to S3 through it). Site-to-Site VPN goes over the internet, and Transit Gateway can't connect to S3.

Kinesis Data Streams absorbs spiky incoming data durably and scales with volume, and Lambda processes it, removing the capacity limit that caused 503 errors. API Gateway quotas would throttle the vendor, and SNS or EC2-only scaling doesn't buffer the load.

A VPC endpoint (gateway endpoint for S3) lets the private-subnet instances reach S3 over the AWS network without the internet, and the bucket policy can restrict access to that endpoint. Internet gateways, NAT gateways, and VPN connections use or involve the internet or aren't the right path.

Enabling secrets encryption on the EKS cluster with a KMS key encrypts Kubernetes secrets at rest in etcd using envelope encryption, a single setting with no application or Lambda code. The other options require custom work.

An ALB in front of the application servers' Auto Scaling group, with the application servers' security group allowing traffic only from the web servers' security group, restricts access to the web tier. PrivateLink or VPC endpoints aren't the right tools here, and network ACLs can't reference security groups or dynamic instances.

CloudWatch Container Insights collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from containerized applications and EKS clusters in one place, including microservices. The plain agent doesn't aggregate and summarize as Container Insights does, and App Mesh and CloudTrail aren't for metrics and logs.

Amazon GuardDuty continuously monitors the account, workloads, and S3 access patterns for malicious activity, and it sends findings to AWS Security Hub for a consolidated dashboard. Macie, Inspector, and Config don't do threat detection across all these sources.

EFS provides a shared NFS file system that multiple AWS resources can mount, and a DataSync agent on premises with a DataSync task migrates the 200 GB without interrupting existing services, and it's cost-effective. FSx for Lustre and S3 aren't NFS file systems for the use case, and manual copying isn't managed.

A Multi-AZ FSx for Windows file system gives high availability for planned maintenance and unplanned disruptions, AWS Backup copies backups to us-west-2, and Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode with a 5-year minimum prevents anyone from deleting the replicated data. Governance mode can be bypassed by privileged users, and Single-AZ lacks the same availability.

An SCP attached to the developer accounts that prohibits changes to CloudTrail applies even to the accounts' root users, so the mandatory trail can't be modified. IAM policies can't restrict the root user, and creating trails within the accounts or service-linked roles don't protect the configuration.

Provisioned IOPS SSD EBS volumes provide durable storage with consistent, low-latency performance for business-critical applications. Instance store isn't durable, ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, and HDD volumes don't offer low latency.

S3 Cross-Region Replication automatically copies new objects from the us-west-1 bucket to a bucket in us-east-1 with no code or ongoing work. CORS isn't replication, and lifecycle rules or Lambda copying add effort.

DynamoDB with on-demand capacity scales instantly for the huge morning spike and supports a flexible schema that can evolve quickly, and storing the static page in S3 behind CloudFront scales to millions of users with no servers. Aurora Serverless and EC2 fleets scale less smoothly or have rigid schemas.

AWS WAF integrates directly with API Gateway and provides managed rules that block SQL injection and cross-site scripting, the most operationally efficient solution. Shield defends against DDoS, and adding CloudFront in front only adds components.

SAML 2.0 federation with the corporate Active Directory lets users sign in with their existing identities, and IAM roles mapped to AD groups grant access to AWS resources, so there's no separate identity to maintain. IAM users for 1,500 people or Cognito or cross-account roles don't map AD groups.

Route 53 geolocation routing serves content based on the user's location (country or continent), so each region is sent to the content it has distribution rights for. Geoproximity routes by distance (and can bias), not by legal boundaries, and WAF or CloudFront alone don't pick content by location this way.
